arguments.explanation: All four parts (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, inverted_u_yellow) reached their placement frames within position and orientation tolerance by run end. u_orange's first insertion attempt caught on the slot edge, leaving it tilted ~23 deg (exceeding its 10 deg tolerance) though still within position tolerance; this was recorded as non_conformant, then corrected by re-grasping and reseating it, verified conformant on the second attempt -- no violation stands at run end for u_orange. Clamp effort monitors (object-specific max_clamp_effort, from registry) were armed for each part while held and none fired. Four bystander stationarity monitors (u_green, inverted_u_brown, hex_blue, hex_red, each using registry disturbance_tolerance_m=0.02) ran for the whole run and none fired; three previously-seated-part stationarity monitors (u_brown, u_orange, line_green, using registry position_m) likewise ran continuously after each part's place step and none fired. base1 (the fixture) and base2 (the other assembly's fixture) have no spec block in the registry, so no clamp/position tolerance exists for them and their stationarity could not be monitored with a verified threshold; this property is unwatched for those two objects, as reported here. A final camera look at run end showed the assembly complete and no unlisted objects in the workspace. No unexpected events were observed during the run, so no observations were recorded. Absence of a monitor fire means no armed, thresholded check was violated; it is not independent proof that base1/base2 never moved.
